context: Parallel coordinates chart showing adversarial audit scores from 5 agents across 84 blocks, with color encoding for inter-agent disagreement (σ) and a mode toggle to view raw scores vs score deltas between calibration rounds
first_impression: Dense but legible — 84 semi-transparent lines across 6 axes create moderate visual complexity that is kept manageable by thoughtful alpha and color encoding.
what_works: Alpha scaling (0.15–0.55 based on line count) prevents the 84-line density from becoming a hairball, and the Tol Sunset diverging palette effectively encodes disagreement level so high-σ blocks visually pop without requiring interaction. Brush-per-axis filtering is structurally sound for progressive disclosure of subsets.
what_doesnt: The legend bar (100px gradient with only 'low'/'high' labels) gives no numeric anchoring — it's unclear what σ values map to the color extremes, weakening the disagreement encoding. In the middle of the chart where axes are closest together, line crossings create a dense tangle that makes individual trajectory tracking difficult without hovering.
